aspects.says: A Stream object can be operated on once; a second operation on it, intermediate or terminal, throws IllegalStateException.
basis: section:A Stream Can Be Consumed Once, So Keep a Supplier, Not the Stream

aspects.says: Each element goes through every stage before the next element is pulled from the source.
basis: section:Each Element Goes Through the Whole Pipeline Before the Next, and Short-Circuiting Stops the Pulling

aspects.says: An ArrayList stream reads the list when the terminal operation runs, so changes made after stream() and before the terminal operation are seen; a CopyOnWriteArrayList stream reads a snapshot taken at stream().
basis: section:The Source Is Read When the Terminal Operation Runs, and Must Not Change Under It

aspects.says: A loop is clearer than a stream when the work must stop early, throw a checked exception or track positions and several totals; return in a forEach lambda only skips one element.
basis: section:A Loop Is Clearer When the Work Stops Early, Throws a Checked Exception, or Updates Several Variables

aspects.says: Modifying an ArrayList source while the terminal operation runs ends in ConcurrentModificationException, for forEach only after every original element was processed, or in skipped and null elements on removal.
basis: section:The Source Is Read When the Terminal Operation Runs, and Must Not Change Under It

aspects.says: Intermediate operations only record stages; nothing in a pipeline runs until a terminal operation is called.
basis: section:Building a Pipeline Runs Nothing; the Terminal Operation Runs It
aspects.reason: a pipeline that never runs gives a test nothing to call; the vertical-order quiz question and the dispatcher practice show when the stages actually run

aspects.says: A short-circuiting operation such as findFirst or anyMatch stops pulling elements once it has its answer, while collecting first or counting reads every element.
basis: section:Each Element Goes Through the Whole Pipeline Before the Next, and Short-Circuiting Stops the Pulling

aspects.says: Code that needs the same pipeline more than once keeps a Supplier<Stream<T>> or a method that builds a new stream on every use, not a stored Stream.
basis: section:A Stream Can Be Consumed Once, So Keep a Supplier, Not the Stream
